summary: Permanently fix .next/cache EACCES that 500s dynamic routes after deploy
description:
Guest /ask (POST /api/query/guest) 500s with 'Something went wrong' after a deploy. Root cause: the runtime systemd unit runs as user 'guru' (deploy/guru-web.service User=guru), but deploy/deploy.sh chowns the release tree to deploy:deploy (line 66 self-heal + line 127), and the CI tarball EXCLUDES .next/cache (deploy.sh line 86). So guru must mkdir .next/cache at runtime inside a deploy-owned .next/ -> EACCES -> Next surfaces it as a request failure on dynamic routes. Manual chown on prod (2026-09-13) patched the live release but every deploy re-breaks it; line 66 even re-clobbers it mid-deploy.

CHOSEN APPROACH: relocate the runtime-writable cache OUT of the release to a stable, guru-owned path, wired through systemd ReadWritePaths, and symlink .next/cache -> that path on every unpack. Release ownership stays deploy:deploy (no change to the self-heal, no mid-deploy ownership window on the live release), and the cache persists across deploys (warm cache, better hit rate). deploy.sh line 66 only touches releases/, so an external /srv/guru-web/next-cache is immune.

REJECTED ALT: flip line 127 chown to guru:guru. Correct in principle but leaves line 66's 'chown -R deploy:deploy releases/' clobbering the still-live release's cache at the start of the next deploy (transient EACCES window on prod), and needs line 66 reworked into a container=deploy / children=guru split. More surface, more risk than the external-dir approach.

NOTE: vps-bootstrap.sh is one-time and prod already exists, so the cache dir + unit edit need a one-time manual apply on prod in addition to landing in the repo (see child tickets).
